# NovoLog vs Fiasp: Getting Mealtime Aspart Timing Right

✓Last reviewed October 20, 2026 · Written by [Dr. George Grunberger](https://www.glpatlas.com/about/#editor) · Medical review: pending — clinician review in progress · [How we review](https://www.glpatlas.com/editorial-policy/)
Insulin aspart comes as NovoLog (NovoRapid in Canada) and faster Fiasp. When to inject each, pen and pump tips, low-sugar safety and cost programs.
3 min read

Key takeaways
NovoLog is injected 5–10 minutes before a meal; Fiasp, a faster version of insulin aspart, at the start of a meal or within 20 minutes after starting. Both are rapid-acting mealtime insulins dosed in units your clinician sets.

## Insulin aspart at a glance

| Generic name | insulin aspart |
| Made by | Novo Nordisk |
| Type | Rapid-acting (mealtime) insulin |
| Form | Vials, pens, cartridges |
| How often | With meals |
| United States | FDA-approved; unbranded insulin aspart is available. |
| Canada | Available in Canada (NovoRapid, Fiasp). |

[Full Insulin aspart reference: uses, dosing, side effects ](https://www.glpatlas.com/drugs/insulin-aspart/)

## Same insulin, different speed

Fiasp adds ingredients that make aspart reach the blood faster. That makes it forgiving if you forget to dose before eating, but it also means less time between injection and the glucose drop. In Canada, NovoLog is sold as NovoRapid. Unbranded aspart is available in the US.

## Pre-bolusing

With NovoLog, the 5–10 minute gap matters: injecting as you sit down can cause an early spike, while injecting much earlier can cause a low before the food arrives. Use your readings to discuss the right timing with your team.Typical time-action profiles from product labels (darker band = peak). Your response can differ — follow your own plan.

## Pen technique

- Check the label and the insulin's appearance before every dose.
- Attach a new needle and do the safety (prime) shot the leaflet describes.
- Inject under the skin and hold the needle in for the time the leaflet says.
- Rotate sites within an area to avoid lumpy skin (lipohypertrophy), which slows absorption.
- Never share pens, even with a new needle.

## Low blood sugar

**Know your low-sugar plan.** Signs include shaking, sweating, a fast heartbeat, hunger, confusion and irritability. A common approach is the rule of 15: take 15 g of fast-acting carbohydrate (glucose tablets, juice or regular soda), recheck after 15 minutes, and repeat if still low. Make sure someone close to you knows how to use rescue glucagon.

## Storage and cost

Unopened: refrigerate. In use: up to 28 days at room temperature.
In the US, Medicare caps insulin out-of-pocket costs at $35 a month, and manufacturers run $35 programs for many people with commercial insurance or none. Check eligibility before paying list price.

## Frequently asked questions

Can I switch from NovoLog to Fiasp myself?

No. Switching changes timing and sometimes dose; do it with your prescriber.Is NovoRapid the same as NovoLog?

Yes — NovoRapid is the Canadian brand name for insulin aspart.Can aspart be used in a pump?

Yes, both are used in pumps; check which your pump is approved for.

# Apidra (Insulin Glulisine): A Practical Mealtime Guide

✓Last reviewed October 20, 2026 · Written by [Dr. George Grunberger](https://www.glpatlas.com/about/#editor) · Medical review: pending — clinician review in progress · [How we review](https://www.glpatlas.com/editorial-policy/)
Using Apidra (insulin glulisine): timing with meals, pens and pumps, how it compares with lispro and aspart, low-sugar safety and storage.
3 min read

Key takeaways
Apidra is a rapid-acting mealtime insulin taken within 15 minutes before or within 20 minutes after starting a meal. It works like lispro and aspart; the choice often comes down to coverage, pen preference and how your body responds.

## Apidra at a glance

| Generic name | insulin glulisine |
| Made by | Sanofi |
| Type | Rapid-acting (mealtime) insulin |
| Form | Vials, pens |
| How often | With meals |
| United States | FDA-approved. |
| Canada | Check the Drug Product Database. |

[Full Apidra reference: uses, dosing, side effects ](https://www.glpatlas.com/drugs/insulin-glulisine/)

## How it compares

All three rapid-acting insulins — lispro, aspart and glulisine — start working within about 15 minutes and last a few hours. Apidra is made by Sanofi and comes in vials and SoloStar pens.

## Using it day to day

Agree a clear plan with your team: a set dose per meal or a carbohydrate ratio, plus a correction rule for high readings. Skipped meal usually means skipped dose.

- Check the label and the insulin's appearance before every dose.
- Attach a new needle and do the safety (prime) shot the leaflet describes.
- Inject under the skin and hold the needle in for the time the leaflet says.
- Rotate sites within an area to avoid lumpy skin (lipohypertrophy), which slows absorption.
- Never share pens, even with a new needle.Typical time-action profiles from product labels (darker band = peak). Your response can differ — follow your own plan.

## Pumps

Apidra can be used in pumps. Ask how often to change the infusion set and what to do if readings rise unexpectedly — a blocked set is a common cause.

## Low blood sugar

**Know your low-sugar plan.** Signs include shaking, sweating, a fast heartbeat, hunger, confusion and irritability. A common approach is the rule of 15: take 15 g of fast-acting carbohydrate (glucose tablets, juice or regular soda), recheck after 15 minutes, and repeat if still low. Make sure someone close to you knows how to use rescue glucagon.

## Storage

Unopened: refrigerate. In use: up to 28 days at room temperature.

## Frequently asked questions

Is Apidra interchangeable with Humalog?

They are different insulins with similar action. Switching should be planned with your prescriber.Can Apidra be mixed with other insulin?

Only as the product labeling allows; ask your pharmacist before mixing any insulins.What if my pharmacy doesn't stock it?

Ask your prescriber whether lispro or aspart is a suitable alternative under your plan.

Title: Regular Insulin (Humulin R, Novolin R): Timing & Cost
Summary: Regular human insulin explained: why it is taken 30 minutes before meals, over-the-counter U-100 vs prescription U-500, safety and low-cost options.
Last reviewed: 2026-10-20

Blog · Insulin
# Regular Insulin (Humulin R, Novolin R): Timing & Cost

✓Last reviewed October 20, 2026 · Written by [Dr. George Grunberger](https://www.glpatlas.com/about/#editor) · Medical review: pending — clinician review in progress · [How we review](https://www.glpatlas.com/editorial-policy/)
Regular human insulin explained: why it is taken 30 minutes before meals, over-the-counter U-100 vs prescription U-500, safety and low-cost options.
3 min read

Key takeaways
Regular insulin is short-acting human insulin taken about 30 minutes before a meal. U-100 Humulin R and Novolin R are sold over the counter at many US pharmacies and are among the cheapest insulins; concentrated Humulin R U-500 needs a prescription.

## Regular insulin at a glance

| Generic name | human insulin (regular) |
| Made by | Eli Lilly; Novo Nordisk |
| Type | Short-acting insulin |
| Form | Vials, pens |
| How often | Before meals |
| United States | FDA-approved. U-100 is sold over the counter at many US pharmacies; Humulin R U-500 requires a prescription. |
| Canada | Available in Canada. |

[Full Regular insulin reference: uses, dosing, side effects ](https://www.glpatlas.com/drugs/regular-insulin/)

## How it differs from rapid-acting insulin

Regular insulin starts more slowly and lasts longer than lispro or aspart. That is why it is injected about half an hour before eating, and why lows can happen several hours after a meal.

## Over the counter — but not without guidance

Being able to buy U-100 regular insulin without a prescription helps in a pinch, but switching from a modern insulin is not unit-for-unit simple. Talk to a clinician or pharmacist before you change, even for a short time.Typical time-action profiles from product labels (darker band = peak). Your response can differ — follow your own plan.

## U-500: a different product

Humulin R U-500 is five times more concentrated. It is prescribed for people who need very large doses and uses its own dedicated pen or syringe. Mix-ups between U-100 and U-500 can cause dangerous lows.

## Low blood sugar

**Know your low-sugar plan.** Signs include shaking, sweating, a fast heartbeat, hunger, confusion and irritability. A common approach is the rule of 15: take 15 g of fast-acting carbohydrate (glucose tablets, juice or regular soda), recheck after 15 minutes, and repeat if still low. Make sure someone close to you knows how to use rescue glucagon.

## Storage

Unopened: refrigerate. In use: follow the product labeling, often 31–42 days.

## Frequently asked questions

Can I inject regular insulin right before eating?

It works best about 30 minutes before a meal. Ask your clinician how to adjust if that is hard to fit into your routine.Is store-brand insulin the same?

Store-brand human insulins are the same regular or NPH insulin sold under a pharmacy brand.Is regular insulin used in emergencies?

Hospitals use it intravenously; at home it is a mealtime insulin.

Title: NPH Insulin: How to Use Cloudy Insulin Safely
Summary: NPH insulin (Humulin N, Novolin N) is cloudy and must be mixed before every dose. How to resuspend it, when it peaks, night-time lows and cost.
Last reviewed: 2026-10-20

Blog · Insulin
# NPH Insulin: How to Use Cloudy Insulin Safely

✓Last reviewed October 20, 2026 · Written by [Dr. George Grunberger](https://www.glpatlas.com/about/#editor) · Medical review: pending — clinician review in progress · [How we review](https://www.glpatlas.com/editorial-policy/)
NPH insulin (Humulin N, Novolin N) is cloudy and must be mixed before every dose. How to resuspend it, when it peaks, night-time lows and cost.
3 min read

Key takeaways
NPH is an intermediate-acting human insulin, used once or twice daily for background control. It is cloudy and must be gently mixed before every dose. Because it peaks several hours after injection, meal and snack timing matter more than with modern basal insulins.

## NPH insulin at a glance

| Generic name | isophane human insulin |
| Made by | Eli Lilly; Novo Nordisk |
| Type | Intermediate-acting insulin |
| Form | Vials, pens |
| How often | Once or twice daily |
| United States | FDA-approved; available over the counter at many US pharmacies. |
| Canada | Available in Canada. |

[Full NPH insulin reference: uses, dosing, side effects ](https://www.glpatlas.com/drugs/nph-insulin/)

## Mix it every time

NPH crystals settle. Roll the vial or pen between your hands and tip it gently, as the instructions describe, until it is evenly cloudy — do not shake hard. An unmixed dose can be too weak or too strong.

## Understanding the peak

NPH has a peak a few hours after injection. If you take it at night, that peak can fall in the early morning hours. Ask your clinician whether you need a bedtime snack or a different timing, and check your sugar overnight if you feel unwell on waking.Typical time-action profiles from product labels (darker band = peak). Your response can differ — follow your own plan.

## Using it with other insulin

NPH is sometimes mixed with regular insulin in the same syringe, drawing clear before cloudy. Only do this if your team has taught you; premixed 70/30 insulins do it for you.

## Low blood sugar

**Know your low-sugar plan.** Signs include shaking, sweating, a fast heartbeat, hunger, confusion and irritability. A common approach is the rule of 15: take 15 g of fast-acting carbohydrate (glucose tablets, juice or regular soda), recheck after 15 minutes, and repeat if still low. Make sure someone close to you knows how to use rescue glucagon.

## Cost

NPH is available over the counter at many US pharmacies and is one of the lowest-cost insulins.

## Frequently asked questions

Why is my NPH cloudy but my other insulin clear?

NPH is a suspension; cloudiness is normal. Clear insulins should never look cloudy.Can NPH replace Lantus?

Sometimes, for cost reasons, but the doses and timing differ. Switch only with your clinician's plan.How many times should I roll the pen?

Follow your product's leaflet; most say to roll and tip it until it looks uniformly white and cloudy.

Title: Lantus, Basaglar, Semglee, Toujeo: Glargine Explained
Summary: All the insulin glargine brands compared: Lantus, Basaglar, Semglee, Rezvoglar and concentrated Toujeo U-300 — switching rules, storage and savings.
Last reviewed: 2026-10-20

Blog · Insulin
# Lantus, Basaglar, Semglee, Toujeo: Glargine Explained

✓Last reviewed October 20, 2026 · Written by [Dr. George Grunberger](https://www.glpatlas.com/about/#editor) · Medical review: pending — clinician review in progress · [How we review](https://www.glpatlas.com/editorial-policy/)
All the insulin glargine brands compared: Lantus, Basaglar, Semglee, Rezvoglar and concentrated Toujeo U-300 — switching rules, storage and savings.
3 min read

Key takeaways
Insulin glargine is a once-daily basal insulin. Lantus, Basaglar, Semglee and Rezvoglar are U-100; Semglee and Rezvoglar are interchangeable biosimilars to Lantus. Toujeo is a concentrated U-300 form that is not unit-for-unit identical when switching.

## Insulin glargine at a glance

| Generic name | insulin glargine |
| Made by | Sanofi; Eli Lilly; Biocon/Viatris |
| Type | Long-acting (basal) insulin |
| Form | Vials, pens |
| How often | Once daily |
| United States | FDA-approved. Semglee and Rezvoglar are interchangeable biosimilars to Lantus. Toujeo is a concentrated U-300 form. Levemir (insulin detemir) has been discontinued in the US. |
| Canada | Available in Canada (including biosimilars). |

[Full Insulin glargine reference: uses, dosing, side effects ](https://www.glpatlas.com/drugs/insulin-glargine/)

## Biosimilars, simply

An interchangeable biosimilar can be swapped for the original at the pharmacy, where state law allows, just like a generic. Semglee and Rezvoglar have that status for Lantus, which often lowers the price.

## Toujeo is different

Toujeo holds three times as much insulin per mL. People switching from U-100 glargine often need a somewhat different dose. Do not convert doses yourself and never draw Toujeo into a regular syringe.Typical time-action profiles from product labels (darker band = peak). Your response can differ — follow your own plan.

## Daily routine

Inject once a day at the same time. Do not dilute glargine or mix it with other insulins.

- Check the label and the insulin's appearance before every dose.
- Attach a new needle and do the safety (prime) shot the leaflet describes.
- Inject under the skin and hold the needle in for the time the leaflet says.
- Rotate sites within an area to avoid lumpy skin (lipohypertrophy), which slows absorption.
- Never share pens, even with a new needle.

## Low blood sugar

**Know your low-sugar plan.** Signs include shaking, sweating, a fast heartbeat, hunger, confusion and irritability. A common approach is the rule of 15: take 15 g of fast-acting carbohydrate (glucose tablets, juice or regular soda), recheck after 15 minutes, and repeat if still low. Make sure someone close to you knows how to use rescue glucagon.

## Storage

Unopened: refrigerate. In use: Lantus up to 28 days, Toujeo up to 56 days at room temperature.
In the US, Medicare caps insulin out-of-pocket costs at $35 a month, and manufacturers run $35 programs for many people with commercial insurance or none. Check eligibility before paying list price.

## What happened to Levemir?

Insulin detemir (Levemir) has been discontinued in the US. If you used it, your prescriber will have moved you to another basal insulin such as glargine or degludec.

## Frequently asked questions

Can I switch from Lantus to Semglee?

Yes, they are interchangeable, and your pharmacist may substitute one for the other where permitted.Morning or night?

Either, as long as it is the same time each day. Your clinician may suggest a time based on your readings.Is glargine safe in type 1 diabetes?

Yes, it is approved for basal control in type 1 and type 2 diabetes.

Title: Tresiba (Degludec): Why Flexible Timing Matters

Last reviewed: 2026-10-20

Blog · Insulin
# Tresiba (Degludec): Why Flexible Timing Matters

✓Last reviewed October 20, 2026 · Written by [Dr. George Grunberger](https://www.glpatlas.com/about/#editor) · Medical review: pending — clinician review in progress · [How we review](https://www.glpatlas.com/editorial-policy/)
Tresiba (insulin degludec) is an ultra-long basal insulin with flexible dose timing. How the 8-hour rule works, U-100 vs U-200 pens, storage and cost.
3 min read

Key takeaways
Tresiba is an ultra-long-acting basal insulin taken once a day. Its long action allows flexible timing — the label only requires at least 8 hours between doses. It comes in U-100 and U-200 pens, and unbranded insulin degludec is available in the US.

## Tresiba at a glance

| Generic name | insulin degludec |
| Made by | Novo Nordisk |
| Type | Ultra-long-acting (basal) insulin |
| Form | Pens (U-100, U-200), vials |
| How often | Once daily |
| United States | FDA-approved; unbranded insulin degludec is available. |
| Canada | Available in Canada. |

[Full Tresiba reference: uses, dosing, side effects ](https://www.glpatlas.com/drugs/insulin-degludec/)

## The flexibility, in practice

If you normally inject at 8 a.m. but forget until lunchtime, you can still take that day's dose, as long as at least 8 hours separate it from the next one. That makes degludec useful for shift workers and travelers.

## U-100 or U-200

U-200 pens hold twice the insulin per mL, so they suit people who need larger doses. The pen counter shows the units you get, so you do not need to convert — but never draw U-200 out of a pen with a syringe.Typical time-action profiles from product labels (darker band = peak). Your response can differ — follow your own plan.

## Who can use it

Tresiba is approved for basal control in diabetes in adults and children aged 1 and older.

## Low blood sugar

**Know your low-sugar plan.** Signs include shaking, sweating, a fast heartbeat, hunger, confusion and irritability. A common approach is the rule of 15: take 15 g of fast-acting carbohydrate (glucose tablets, juice or regular soda), recheck after 15 minutes, and repeat if still low. Make sure someone close to you knows how to use rescue glucagon.

## Storage

Unopened: refrigerate. In use: up to 56 days at room temperature or in the fridge.
In the US, Medicare caps insulin out-of-pocket costs at $35 a month, and manufacturers run $35 programs for many people with commercial insurance or none. Check eligibility before paying list price.

## Frequently asked questions

Can I take Tresiba at a different time every day?

Yes, within the label's rule of at least 8 hours between doses. A regular time still helps you remember.Tresiba or glargine?

Both are basal insulins; degludec lasts longer and allows more flexible timing. Coverage often decides.Why does it take days for dose changes to show?

Because it is so long-acting, it takes a few days to reach a steady level after each change.

Title: Awiqli: What Once-Weekly Insulin Changes for You
Summary: Awiqli (insulin icodec) is the first once-weekly basal insulin in the US. Who it is for, how switching from daily insulin works, and what to watch for.
Last reviewed: 2026-10-20

Blog · Insulin
# Awiqli: What Once-Weekly Insulin Changes for You

✓Last reviewed October 20, 2026 · Written by [Dr. George Grunberger](https://www.glpatlas.com/about/#editor) · Medical review: pending — clinician review in progress · [How we review](https://www.glpatlas.com/editorial-policy/)
Awiqli (insulin icodec) is the first once-weekly basal insulin in the US. Who it is for, how switching from daily insulin works, and what to watch for.
3 min read

Key takeaways
Awiqli replaces seven daily basal injections with one weekly shot. The FDA approved it on March 26, 2026 for adults with type 2 diabetes — not for type 1. Switching from daily insulin follows specific label instructions, so let your prescriber set the first doses.

## Awiqli at a glance

| Generic name | insulin icodec-abae |
| Made by | Novo Nordisk |
| Type | Once-weekly basal insulin (700 units/mL) |
| Form | FlexTouch prefilled pen |
| How often | Once weekly |
| United States | FDA-approved March 26, 2026 — the first once-weekly basal insulin in the US; launched in 2026. Not approved for type 1 diabetes. |
| Canada | Approved in Canada and the EU earlier than in the US. |

[Full Awiqli reference: uses, dosing, side effects ](https://www.glpatlas.com/drugs/insulin-icodec/)

## Who it is for

Adults with type 2 diabetes who need basal insulin. For people who dislike daily injections or forget them, a weekly dose can make treatment easier to stick with.

## How it is different

Icodec is highly concentrated (700 units/mL) and binds in the blood, releasing slowly over the week. Dose changes take time to show, so adjustments are usually made weekly rather than daily.Typical time-action profiles from product labels (darker band = peak). Your response can differ — follow your own plan.

## Switching from daily insulin

The label has a specific method for the first injection after daily basal insulin. Do not convert doses yourself. Plan more glucose checks in the first weeks.

## Low blood sugar

**Know your low-sugar plan.** Signs include shaking, sweating, a fast heartbeat, hunger, confusion and irritability. A common approach is the rule of 15: take 15 g of fast-acting carbohydrate (glucose tablets, juice or regular soda), recheck after 15 minutes, and repeat if still low. Make sure someone close to you knows how to use rescue glucagon.

## Cost and coverage

Pricing and insurance coverage were still settling after launch. Check your plan and the manufacturer's programs before you fill.

## Frequently asked questions

Can I use Awiqli for type 1 diabetes?

No — in the US it is approved only for adults with type 2 diabetes.Which day should I inject?

Pick one day and keep it every week, as your prescriber advises.Is it available in Canada?

Yes — insulin icodec was approved in Canada and the EU before the US.

Title: Premixed Insulin 70/30 and Mixes: Who They Suit
Summary: Premixed insulins (Humulin and Novolin 70/30, Humalog Mix, NovoLog Mix) explained: what the numbers mean, meal timing, mixing technique and cost.
Last reviewed: 2026-10-20

Blog · Insulin
# Premixed Insulin 70/30 and Mixes: Who They Suit

✓Last reviewed October 20, 2026 · Written by [Dr. George Grunberger](https://www.glpatlas.com/about/#editor) · Medical review: pending — clinician review in progress · [How we review](https://www.glpatlas.com/editorial-policy/)
Premixed insulins (Humulin and Novolin 70/30, Humalog Mix, NovoLog Mix) explained: what the numbers mean, meal timing, mixing technique and cost.
3 min read

Key takeaways
Premixed insulins combine an intermediate-acting insulin with a rapid- or short-acting one in a fixed ratio, usually injected twice a day with meals. They suit people with regular meal times who want fewer injections. 70/30 human insulin is among the cheapest options.

## Premixed insulin at a glance

| Generic name | premixed insulin |
| Made by | Eli Lilly; Novo Nordisk |
| Type | Premixed (intermediate + rapid or short) |
| Form | Vials, pens |
| How often | Usually twice daily with meals |
| United States | FDA-approved. |
| Canada | Available in Canada. |

[Full Premixed insulin reference: uses, dosing, side effects ](https://www.glpatlas.com/drugs/premixed-insulin/)

## What the numbers mean

In 70/30, 70% of the insulin is intermediate-acting and 30% short- or rapid-acting. Humalog Mix 75/25 and NovoLog Mix 70/30 use modern rapid-acting insulins; Humulin and Novolin 70/30 use human insulin.

## Routine matters

Because each dose covers a meal and the hours after it, regular meals are important. Skipping a meal after a premixed dose can cause a low. Ask how to handle late or small meals.Typical time-action profiles from product labels (darker band = peak). Your response can differ — follow your own plan.

## Mixing technique

Premixed insulins are cloudy suspensions. Roll and tip the pen or vial gently until evenly cloudy before every dose.

- Check the label and the insulin's appearance before every dose.
- Attach a new needle and do the safety (prime) shot the leaflet describes.
- Inject under the skin and hold the needle in for the time the leaflet says.
- Rotate sites within an area to avoid lumpy skin (lipohypertrophy), which slows absorption.
- Never share pens, even with a new needle.

## Low blood sugar

**Know your low-sugar plan.** Signs include shaking, sweating, a fast heartbeat, hunger, confusion and irritability. A common approach is the rule of 15: take 15 g of fast-acting carbohydrate (glucose tablets, juice or regular soda), recheck after 15 minutes, and repeat if still low. Make sure someone close to you knows how to use rescue glucagon.

## Storage and cost

Unopened: refrigerate. In use: follow the product labeling. Human-insulin 70/30 is available over the counter at many US pharmacies at low cost.

## Frequently asked questions

Is Humalog Mix the same as Humulin 70/30?

No. They contain different insulins with different timing; do not swap them without your prescriber.When do I inject?

Timing depends on the product — modern mixes close to the meal, human 70/30 about 30 minutes before. Follow your label and plan.Can I adjust the ratio?

No. The ratio is fixed; if you need more flexibility, separate basal and mealtime insulins may suit you better.

Title: Symlin (Pramlintide): Using It Safely With Insulin
Summary: Symlin (pramlintide) is an amylin analog added to mealtime insulin. Why insulin doses are cut at the start, how to avoid severe lows, and injection rules.
Last reviewed: 2026-10-20

Blog · Rescue & add-on
# Symlin (Pramlintide): Using It Safely With Insulin

✓Last reviewed October 20, 2026 · Written by [Dr. George Grunberger](https://www.glpatlas.com/about/#editor) · Medical review: pending — clinician review in progress · [How we review](https://www.glpatlas.com/editorial-policy/)
Symlin (pramlintide) is an amylin analog added to mealtime insulin. Why insulin doses are cut at the start, how to avoid severe lows, and injection rules.
3 min read

Key takeaways
Symlin is injected before major meals alongside mealtime insulin in type 1 or type 2 diabetes. It carries a boxed warning for severe low blood sugar, so mealtime insulin is usually reduced at the start and glucose is checked often.

## Symlin at a glance

| Generic name | pramlintide |
| Made by | AstraZeneca |
| Type | Amylin analog |
| Form | Pen injection |
| How often | Before major meals |
| United States | FDA-approved. |
| Canada | Not marketed in Canada as far as public listings show; check the Drug Product Database. |

[Full Symlin reference: uses, dosing, side effects ](https://www.glpatlas.com/drugs/symlin/)

## What amylin does

Amylin is released with insulin after meals. Pramlintide mimics it: it slows stomach emptying, lowers glucagon after meals and increases fullness. The result is a smaller glucose rise after eating.

## The boxed warning

Severe hypoglycemia can happen, especially in type 1 diabetes, usually within a few hours of the injection. Starting low, reducing mealtime insulin and checking glucose before and after meals are the safeguards. Do not drive or operate machinery until you know how it affects you.The main actions of pramlintide, an amylin analog used with mealtime insulin.

## Injection rules

- Inject before major meals only — skip it if you skip the meal.
- Never mix Symlin with insulin in the same syringe; use separate sites.
- Your dose in micrograms is set and increased by your prescriber.

## Low blood sugar

**Know your low-sugar plan.** Signs include shaking, sweating, a fast heartbeat, hunger, confusion and irritability. A common approach is the rule of 15: take 15 g of fast-acting carbohydrate (glucose tablets, juice or regular soda), recheck after 15 minutes, and repeat if still low. Make sure someone close to you knows how to use rescue glucagon.

## Availability

Symlin is brand-only in the US and does not appear to be marketed in Canada; check the Drug Product Database.
**⚠ Boxed warning: severe low blood sugar with insulin, especially in type 1 diabetes.**

## Frequently asked questions

Can I use Symlin without insulin?

No. It is approved only as an add-on to mealtime insulin.Does Symlin cause weight loss?

It can reduce appetite, but it is approved for blood sugar control, not weight management.What if I feel sick after starting?

Nausea is common at first. Tell your prescriber — the dose may be kept lower for longer.

Title: Glucagon Rescue: Gvoke, Baqsimi, GlucaGen — Be Ready
Summary: Rescue glucagon for severe low blood sugar: nasal Baqsimi, Gvoke and Zegalogue pens, GlucaGen kits — how each works, who should carry one, and what to do after.
Last reviewed: 2026-10-20

Blog · Rescue & add-on
# Glucagon Rescue: Gvoke, Baqsimi, GlucaGen — Be Ready

✓Last reviewed October 20, 2026 · Written by [Dr. George Grunberger](https://www.glpatlas.com/about/#editor) · Medical review: pending — clinician review in progress · [How we review](https://www.glpatlas.com/editorial-policy/)
Rescue glucagon for severe low blood sugar: nasal Baqsimi, Gvoke and Zegalogue pens, GlucaGen kits — how each works, who should carry one, and what to do after.
3 min read

Key takeaways
Rescue glucagon treats severe low blood sugar when someone cannot safely eat or drink. Modern options — a nasal powder (Baqsimi) and ready-to-use pens or syringes (Gvoke, Zegalogue) — are much simpler than the old mixing kits. After giving it, call emergency services.

## Glucagon at a glance

| Generic name | glucagon / dasiglucagon |
| Made by | Various |
| Type | Emergency treatment for severe low blood sugar |
| Form | Injection kit, prefilled pen/syringe, nasal powder (Baqsimi) |
| How often | Emergency use only |
| United States | FDA-approved; several generics. |
| Canada | Available in Canada. |

[Full Glucagon reference: uses, dosing, side effects ](https://www.glpatlas.com/drugs/glucagon/)

## Who should have one

Anyone using insulin — and many people taking sulfonylureas — should ask about a rescue glucagon prescription. It is used by a family member, friend, coworker or teacher, so they need to know where it is and how it works.

## The options

- **Baqsimi:** a nasal powder sprayed into one nostril; no needle and no inhaling needed.
- **Gvoke:** a prefilled pen or syringe, injected under the skin.
- **Zegalogue (dasiglucagon):** a ready-to-use autoinjector or syringe.
- **GlucaGen and generic kits:** powder that must be mixed before injecting.General emergency steps — always follow the instructions supplied with your glucagon product.

## Step by step in an emergency

- Give the glucagon following the device's own instructions.
- Call 911 (US/Canada).
- Turn the person on their side — they may vomit as they recover.
- Once awake and able to swallow, give fast sugar, then a snack.

## Keep it ready

Store at room temperature and check the expiry date every few months. Keep one at home and one in a bag or at school or work. Practice with a trainer device if one is available.

## Cost

Generic and brand options exist, and insurance usually covers rescue glucagon. Ask about two-packs so you can keep one in each place.

## Frequently asked questions

Can glucagon be given if I'm not sure the sugar is low?

If the person is unconscious or cannot swallow and has diabetes treated with insulin, giving glucagon and calling 911 is the standard advice.Does nasal glucagon work if I have a cold?

Studies supported its use during colds and congestion; follow the product label.What happens after glucagon?

The person usually wakes within about 15 minutes. They still need emergency care and food once they can swallow.

Title: CagriSema in 2026: FDA Review, Trials and Timing

# CagriSema in 2026: FDA Review, Trials and Timing

✓Last reviewed October 20, 2026 · Written by [Dr. George Grunberger](https://www.glpatlas.com/about/#editor) · Medical review: pending — clinician review in progress · [How we review](https://www.glpatlas.com/editorial-policy/)
CagriSema (cagrilintide + semaglutide) in 2026: the December 2025 FDA filing, REDEFINE trial results, expected decision and why online versions are fake.
3 min read

Key takeaways
CagriSema combines the amylin analog cagrilintide with semaglutide in one weekly injection. Novo Nordisk filed it with the FDA on December 18, 2025 and expects a decision in Q4 2026. Until approval, it cannot legally be bought — anything sold online is not the real product.

## CagriSema at a glance

| Generic name | cagrilintide + semaglutide |
| Made by | Novo Nordisk |
| Type | Amylin analog + GLP-1 receptor agonist combination |
| Form | Weekly injection |
| How often | Once weekly |
| United States | Not FDA-approved. Filed December 18, 2025; Novo Nordisk guides to an FDA decision in Q4 2026. |
| Canada | Not approved. |

[Full CagriSema reference: uses, dosing, side effects ](https://www.glpatlas.com/drugs/cagrisema/)

## How it works

Semaglutide acts on GLP-1 receptors; cagrilintide mimics amylin, another fullness hormone. Acting on both pathways is designed to reduce appetite more than either alone.

## What the trials showed

In the phase 3 REDEFINE 1 trial in adults with obesity, average weight loss was around 20–23% after 68 weeks, depending on the analysis. Gastrointestinal side effects were the most common, as with other incretin medicines.The four main actions of GLP-1 receptor agonists, as described on their labels.

## Timeline

- December 18, 2025: submitted to the FDA for chronic weight management.
- Q4 2026: decision expected, according to Novo Nordisk.
- Canada: not approved.

## Avoid “research” CagriSema

Websites selling cagrilintide or CagriSema “for research” are not selling an approved medicine. The FDA has warned sellers of unapproved GLP-1 products. If you want access now, the only legal route is a registered clinical trial.

## Frequently asked questions

When will CagriSema be available?

Only after FDA approval; Novo Nordisk expects a decision in Q4 2026, and launch would follow.Will it be stronger than Wegovy?

Trial results suggest more average weight loss than semaglutide alone, but direct comparisons and the final label will decide.Can I join a trial?

Search ClinicalTrials.gov for cagrilintide studies near you.

Blog · Pipeline
# Retatrutide in 2026: Trial Results and What's Next

✓Last reviewed October 20, 2026 · Written by [Dr. George Grunberger](https://www.glpatlas.com/about/#editor) · Medical review: pending — clinician review in progress · [How we review](https://www.glpatlas.com/editorial-policy/)
Retatrutide, Lilly's GIP/GLP-1/glucagon triple agonist: TRIUMPH phase 3 results from July 2026, the planned 2027 FDA filing, and why online 'reta' is unsafe.
3 min read

Key takeaways
Retatrutide is an investigational weekly injection that acts on three hormone receptors: GIP, GLP-1 and glucagon. Lilly reported positive TRIUMPH-2 and TRIUMPH-3 phase 3 results in July 2026 and plans to submit to the FDA in Q1 2027. It is not approved anywhere.

## Retatrutide at a glance

| Generic name | retatrutide |
| Made by | Eli Lilly |
| Type | GIP / GLP-1 / glucagon triple receptor agonist |
| Form | Weekly injection |
| How often | Once weekly |
| United States | Not FDA-approved. Lilly plans to submit to the FDA in Q1 2027 after positive TRIUMPH-2 and TRIUMPH-3 results (July 2026). |
| Canada | Not approved. |

[Full Retatrutide reference: uses, dosing, side effects ](https://www.glpatlas.com/drugs/retatrutide/)

## Why a triple agonist

Adding glucagon-receptor activity to GIP and GLP-1 is designed to increase energy use as well as reduce appetite. In the phase 2 trial, the highest dose produced average weight loss of about 24% at 48 weeks.

## What is being studied

The TRIUMPH phase 3 program covers obesity, knee osteoarthritis pain and obstructive sleep apnea, among other conditions.The four main actions of GLP-1 receptor agonists, as described on their labels.

## Timeline

- July 2026: positive TRIUMPH-2 and TRIUMPH-3 results announced.
- Q1 2027: planned FDA submission.
- Approval would follow review — typically months later.

## Why online “reta” is dangerous

Products sold as retatrutide online are unapproved, untested and of unknown content and dose. In August 2026 the FDA issued warning letters to online sellers of products marketed as retatrutide. Do not inject anything bought this way.

## Frequently asked questions

Is retatrutide approved?

No. It is investigational, with an FDA submission planned for Q1 2027.How is it different from tirzepatide?

Tirzepatide acts on GIP and GLP-1; retatrutide adds glucagon receptors.How can I get it legally?

Only through a registered clinical trial — search ClinicalTrials.gov.

About GLP Atlas
# About us

✓Last reviewed October 20, 2026 · Written by [Dr. George Grunberger](https://www.glpatlas.com/about/#editor) · Medical review: pending — clinician review in progress · [How we review](https://www.glpatlas.com/editorial-policy/)
GLP Atlas is an independent reference on GLP-1, incretin and insulin medicines for readers in the United States and Canada. We explain what each medicine is approved for, how it is dosed according to its official label, its risks, and the legal ways to obtain it.

**We do not sell, ship or broker medicines.** We never process orders and never ask readers to contact us to buy anything.

## Who writes and reviews the content

- **Editor:** Dr. George Grunberger — responsible for every page and every update.

- **Medical review:** pending — clinician review in progress.

- **Last site-wide review:** October 20, 2026.

## What we cover

- 26 GLP-1, incretin, insulin and emergency diabetes medicines, plus two pipeline drugs.

- Side-by-side comparisons, buying guides for the US and Canada, and short answers to common questions.

- Prices, approvals and generics that change often — each page shows the date it was last checked.

## How we work

Facts come from primary sources: FDA and Health Canada labels, manufacturer releases and peer-reviewed trials. We do not publish anonymous claims or user testimonials. Read the full [editorial policy](https://www.glpatlas.com/editorial-policy/).

## Contact

Corrections and editorial questions: [contact@glpatlas.com](https://www.glpatlas.commailto:contact@glpatlas.com). General enquiries: [glp1atlas@gmail.com](https://www.glpatlas.commailto:glp1atlas@gmail.com).

## Sources

Checked against these primary sources on October 20, 2026.

- [Drugs@FDA — approval history and labels](https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/scripts/cder/daf/)
- [Health Canada Drug Product Database](https://health-products.canada.ca/dpd-bdpp/)
- [DailyMed — FDA prescribing information (NIH)](https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/)

Title: Editorial Policy: How We Research and Review
Summary: How GLP Atlas researches, writes, reviews, dates and corrects every page about GLP-1 and diabetes medicines.
Last reviewed: 2026-10-20

About GLP Atlas
# Editorial policy

✓Last reviewed October 20, 2026 · Written by [Dr. George Grunberger](https://www.glpatlas.com/about/#editor) · Medical review: pending — clinician review in progress · [How we review](https://www.glpatlas.com/editorial-policy/)
Every page on GLP Atlas follows the same process. The goal is simple: accurate, current, label-based information you can check yourself.

## Sources we use

- FDA prescribing information (DailyMed and Drugs@FDA) and the Health Canada Drug Product Database.

- Manufacturer press releases for approvals, launches and self-pay prices.

- Peer-reviewed trials and registered studies on ClinicalTrials.gov.

## Review and dates

- Each drug page is reviewed by a licensed clinician before publication and on every major update. The reviewer's name and date appear on the page.

- Pages carry a "last reviewed" date and are re-checked when labels or prices change.

- Dosing is reproduced from the label only. Insulin doses are never given as numbers, because they are always individual.

## Independence

- Commercial partners never see or approve content before publication.

- We do not accept payment to rank, praise or omit any product.

## Corrections

Email [contact@glpatlas.com](https://www.glpatlas.commailto:contact@glpatlas.com). We respond within 5 business days, fix confirmed errors and update the review date.

## Sources

Checked against these primary sources on October 20, 2026.

- [Drugs@FDA — approval history and labels](https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/scripts/cder/daf/)
- [Health Canada Drug Product Database](https://health-products.canada.ca/dpd-bdpp/)
- [DailyMed — FDA prescribing information (NIH)](https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/)
- [ClinicalTrials.gov — registered trials](https://clinicaltrials.gov/)

Title: Medical Disclaimer: Information, Not Medical Advice
Summary: GLP Atlas provides general information about GLP-1 and diabetes medicines. It is not medical advice and does not replace your clinician.
Last reviewed: 2026-10-20

About GLP Atlas
# Medical disclaimer

✓Last reviewed October 20, 2026 · Written by [Dr. George Grunberger](https://www.glpatlas.com/about/#editor) · Medical review: pending — clinician review in progress · [How we review](https://www.glpatlas.com/editorial-policy/)
Content on GLP Atlas is for general information only and is not a substitute for advice from your doctor or pharmacist. Do not start, stop or change a medicine based on this site. In an emergency call 911 (US/Canada).

## What this site can and cannot do

- It can explain what the official label says, in plain English.

- It cannot tell you which medicine or dose is right for you.

- It cannot diagnose a condition or interpret your test results.

## Information changes

Approvals, prices and availability change often. Each page shows the date it was last reviewed. Always check the current label and ask your pharmacist.

## Side effects

If you think you have a side effect, contact your prescriber. You can also report it to the FDA (MedWatch) or Health Canada (MedEffect).

## Sources

Checked against these primary sources on October 20, 2026.

- [FDA MedWatch — report a side effect](https://www.fda.gov/safety/medwatch-fda-safety-information-and-adverse-event-reporting-program)
- [Health Canada MedEffect — report a side effect](https://www.canada.ca/en/health-canada/services/drugs-health-products/medeffect-canada.html)

Title: Affiliate Disclosure: How GLP Atlas Is Funded
Summary: How GLP Atlas makes money, which partners we accept, and why commissions never change our medical content.
Last reviewed: 2026-10-20

About GLP Atlas
# Affiliate disclosure

✓Last reviewed October 20, 2026 · Written by [Dr. George Grunberger](https://www.glpatlas.com/about/#editor) · Medical review: pending — clinician review in progress · [How we review](https://www.glpatlas.com/editorial-policy/)
GLP Atlas may earn a commission when readers use links to licensed telehealth services or pharmacies. Commissions never affect our medical content.

## Our rules for partners

- They must require a valid prescription.

- They must be verified — for example LegitScript-certified or listed on safe.pharmacy.

- They never sell compounded, "research" or foreign-labelled GLP-1 products.

- Paid links are marked and use rel="sponsored".

## No influence on content

Partners do not see pages before publication and cannot ask for changes. Questions: [contact@glpatlas.com](https://www.glpatlas.commailto:contact@glpatlas.com).

## Sources

Checked against these primary sources on October 20, 2026.

- [LegitScript — healthcare merchant certification](https://www.legitscript.com/)
- [NABP safe.pharmacy — verify an online pharmacy](https://safe.pharmacy/)

Title: Privacy Policy: What Data GLP Atlas Collects

About GLP Atlas
# Privacy policy

✓Last reviewed October 20, 2026 · Written by [Dr. George Grunberger](https://www.glpatlas.com/about/#editor) · Medical review: pending — clinician review in progress · [How we review](https://www.glpatlas.com/editorial-policy/)
We collect as little data as possible. We do not sell personal data, and we do not use advertising trackers.

## What we collect

- **Contact form:** your name, email and message, only so we can reply. It is processed by our host's form service.

- **Server logs:** our host keeps standard technical logs (IP address, browser, pages requested) for security.

- **Your device:** we store your light/dark theme choice in your browser's local storage. No cookies are set.

## Share buttons

Share links open WhatsApp, Facebook, LinkedIn or X only when you click them. Those services then apply their own privacy policies.

## Your rights

You can ask to see or delete any message you sent us. Email [contact@glpatlas.com](https://www.glpatlas.commailto:contact@glpatlas.com); we reply within 30 days. US and Canadian privacy laws (including CCPA and PIPEDA) apply.

## Sources

Checked against these primary sources on October 20, 2026.

- [Netlify privacy policy (our host)](https://www.netlify.com/privacy/)
